Event: Your CEO tweeted "our croissants beat therapy" at 3 a.m.
Decision 2: Post a formal apology on LinkedIn
Outcome 1: The hashtag trends all morning!
Outcome 2: Nobody asked for an apology. Now everyone is confused.
Outcome 3: Too late: 40 screenshots are already circulating.

Event: A delivery drone drops a croissant on a famous food critic's head.
Decision 3: Send her a free box every week for a year
Outcome 1: The internet does not buy it.
Outcome 2: The video reaches 3 million views. You are the villain.
Outcome 3: She writes: "Assault by pastry, but delicious."

Event: A cat influencer with 2 million followers wants to review your croissants.
Outcome 1: The cat sniffs the box and leaves. Polite success.
Outcome 2: The owner posts a sad video. Cat lovers are furious.
Outcome 3: The cat licks one croissant. Sales explode.

Event: Your AI-generated ad shows a hand with six fingers holding a croissant.
Decision 1: Lean into it: "Six fingers, twice the croissants"
Decision 2: Say nothing and hope nobody counts
Decision 3: Pull the ad and redo it
Outcome 1: People love brands that laugh at themselves.
Outcome 2: Everybody counts. Memes everywhere.
Outcome 3: Safe, clean, expensive.

Event: A 1-star review: "My croissant arrived by drone. I wanted it by hand."
Decision 2: Explain that drones are the future
Outcome 1: The customer is happy, nobody else notices.
Outcome 2: You sound like a robot. A grumpy one.
Outcome 3: Your reply gets more likes than the review.

Event: Competitor Baguette Bullet launches drones twice as fast as yours.
Decision 1: Make an ad mocking their drones
Decision 2: Film your bakers at 4 a.m.: quality over speed
Decision 3: Start a price war: -30% on everything
Outcome 1: People find it petty.
Outcome 2: The video is beautiful. Butter, flour, sunrise.
Outcome 3: Customers love it. Your accountant cries.

Event: Black Friday is coming.
Decision 2: Skip it: "we bake, we don't discount"
Outcome 1: Sold out in two hours.
Outcome 2: A few people respect that. Quietly.
Outcome 3: Orders explode, quality drops, reviews too.

Event: A TikTok trend: people try to catch your croissants mid-air from the drones.
Outcome 1: Responsible. Slightly boring.
Outcome 2: TikTok does not even reply. Everyone else laughs.
Outcome 3: Best catch wins a year of croissants. Huge buzz.

Event: A data breach: 5,000 customer addresses have leaked.
Decision 1: Notify everyone and fix your security
Decision 2: Notify everyone, fix it, and offer a free croissant
Outcome 1: Painful, but people trust you a bit more.
Outcome 2: The best apology is warm and buttery.
Outcome 3: Journalists disagree. Loudly.

Event: An intern posts a meme on the official account by mistake. 300,000 likes.
Decision 1: Promote the intern to Chief Meme Officer
Outcome 1: The intern is now more famous than your CEO.
Outcome 2: Mysterious. It works, sort of.
Outcome 3: Fans want the meme back.

Event: A celebrity is photographed eating one of your croissants.
Outcome 1: Expensive, but your logo is now on prime time TV.
Outcome 2: Clever and cheap. Marketing at its best.
Outcome 3: Some people notice. Nice.

Event: Drone battery failure: 200 Sunday orders lost.
Decision 1: Refund everyone and post an apology video
Outcome 1: Honest, human, appreciated.
Outcome 2: The others complain about that too.
Outcome 3: It was sunny. Everyone checked.

Event: Your Google Ads campaign has a 0.3% CTR and is burning cash.
Decision 1: Pause it and rewrite the ads
Decision 2: Move the budget to Instagram Stories
Decision 3: Double the budget, it will pick up
Outcome 1: Better ads, smaller bill.
Outcome 2: Croissants look better in vertical video.
Outcome 3: It did not pick up.

Event: A newspaper asks: are drone-delivered croissants bad for the planet?
Decision 2: Run an ad full of trees and sunsets
Outcome 1: Transparency wins you serious respect.
Outcome 2: Greenwashing detected in 12 minutes.
Outcome 3: The headline writes itself.

Event: A fan draws a croissant-shaped drone. The drawing goes viral.
Decision 1: Buy the design to sell T-shirts
Decision 3: Share it and credit the artist
Outcome 1: The T-shirts sell out. The artist gets paid.
Outcome 2: You just attacked a fan. Bad idea.
Outcome 3: The artist is thrilled. So are your fans.

Event: A traditional bakery accuses you of killing small bakeries.
Outcome 1: Your drones now deliver their bread too.
Outcome 2: Silence looks like guilt.
Outcome 3: You hold your ground. Nobody really wins.

Event: Your newsletter typo: "Fresh croissants, delivered by drunk".
Decision 1: Follow-up: "Our drones are sober, we promise"
Outcome 1: Best open rate of the year.
Outcome 2: Some customers are now worried about the pilots.
Outcome 3: Fine. Forgettable.

Event: An investor wants you to use cheaper butter.
Decision 2: Test it secretly on one product
Outcome 1: The investor leaves. Your fans cheer.
Outcome 2: A food blogger finds out. Butter-gate begins.
Outcome 3: Customers taste the difference within a week.

Event: A video shows a pigeon riding one of your drones.
Outcome 1: Serious. Responsible. Zero likes.
Outcome 2: The pigeon flies away. So does the buzz.
Outcome 3: Captain Pigeon gets his own merch line.

Event: An agency offers 50,000 fake followers for 500 EUR.
Decision 2: Report the agency to the platform
Outcome 1: Integrity costs nothing today.
Outcome 2: You get a thank-you note and some press.
Outcome 3: A journalist spots the fake accounts.

Event: Valentine's Day is next week.
Outcome 1: Singles everywhere feel seen.
Outcome 2: Just another Tuesday.
Outcome 3: Couples love them. Instagram loves them more.

Event: A neighborhood complains about drone noise.
Decision 2: Give every neighbor a free croissant
Outcome 1: Silence is golden. And expensive.
Outcome 2: Complaints turn into orders.
Outcome 3: Now they complain at 2 a.m.

Event: A LinkedIn guru calls you "the Uber of pastries".
Decision 1: Invite him to visit the bakery
Decision 2: Reply: "We're more the croissant of croissants"
Outcome 1: He posts 14 selfies with flour on his face.
Outcome 2: Nobody understands. Everybody shares.
Outcome 3: Your mum likes the post.

Event: Your website crashes during a live TV mention.
Decision 1: Put up a "Rocket refueling" page with a promo code
Decision 3: Blame your host on social media
Outcome 1: The waiting page goes viral.
Outcome 2: Back online. Moment missed.
Outcome 3: Customers don't care whose fault it is.

Event: A customer had an allergic reaction: the allergen is missing from your product page.
Decision 3: Update the labels and call the customer
Outcome 1: There was no small print. Disaster.
Outcome 2: Safe, but customers miss it.
Outcome 3: Fast, caring, fixed.

Event: A comedian posts a parody of your latest ad.
Decision 1: Share it and thank the creator
Decision 2: Hire the comedian for your next ad
Decision 3: Ask for it to be removed
Outcome 1: Good sport! Your followers love it.
Outcome 2: The new ad is the funniest of the year.
Outcome 3: The Streisand effect: now everyone has seen it.

Event: Supplier delay: no almonds for a week.
Decision 1: Announce an "almond-free week" with a discount
Decision 2: Launch a "mystery croissant" of the day
Decision 3: Sell plain croissants as almond ones
Outcome 1: Honest and kind of charming.
Outcome 2: People love surprises.
Outcome 3: Customers notice. Of course they notice.

Event: A rival posts fake bad reviews about you.
Decision 3: Post fake good reviews in return
Outcome 1: The platform removes the fake reviews.
Outcome 2: You win. Eventually. Expensively.
Outcome 3: Now both brands look terrible.

Event: A radio show wants your CEO live at 6 a.m.
Decision 1: Send the head baker with fresh croissants
Outcome 1: The hosts eat live. Pure radio gold.
Outcome 2: They invite Baguette Bullet instead.
Outcome 3: He falls asleep live on air.

Event: End of quarter: the board wants growth, now.
Decision 1: Referral program: bring a friend, get a croissant
Outcome 1: Customers become your sales team.
Outcome 2: Revenue up, love down.
Outcome 3: Growth, yes. Profit, no.

Event: A drone lands in the middle of a wedding cake, live on Instagram.
Decision 1: Pay for a new cake and send a croissant tower
Decision 2: Claim it was a planned "surprise delivery"
Decision 3: Offer the couple free croissants for a year
Outcome 1: The bride posts a thank-you video. Guests order for their own weddings.
Outcome 2: The groom's uncle is a lawyer. He is not amused.
Outcome 3: Cute gesture. The couple tags you every Sunday.

Event: A gaming streamer promises to eat only your croissants during a 24-hour live stream.
Decision 2: Send a free box and a thank-you note
Decision 3: Ask him to stop: "croissants are not a full meal"
Outcome 1: Chat spams croissant emojis for 24 hours straight.
Outcome 2: He opens the box on camera. Smiles all round.
Outcome 3: Viewers call you the fun police.

Event: Your drones are spotted delivering croissants to Baguette Bullet's office.
Outcome 1: Your reply becomes the meme of the week.
Outcome 2: They post an empty plate. You look petty.
Outcome 3: They order every morning now. Business is business.
